title: Is there any good Ai-based game engines for mobile?
author: clickii365official

comments.author: RobleyTheron
comments.body: Any reason you don't want to use the main game engines (Godot, Unity or Unreal)? They're all moving quickly to integrate more AI control capabilities. I've used both Godot and Unreal with AI only managing everything and they're doing a really good job. I'm not sure that you need something custom.

replies.author: FazedEclipse2
replies.body: Whats giving you the best output?

replies.author: RobleyTheron
replies.body: Unity, but is the most processor heavy to run.

comments.author: unfamily_friendly
comments.body: Godot. It can mobile. Every file is a non encrypted, human readable text file. And it's an open source, AI could read sources if something doesn't work.

comments.author: Bluetails_Buizel
comments.body: Single file html, and ask it to make a game using 3js for 3D based games

replies.author: RobleyTheron
replies.body: I’ve done this too and it works great!

comments.author: SylvanCreatures
comments.body: Do you need the overhead of an “engine” vs building the game in native code? Godot is pretty awesome, and Claude and ChatGPT are both pretty excellent at using it. Unity is pretty good at mobile, Unreal is ok if you shutoff 80% of its features. I am not aware of any specific “AI engines”, just good integrations into existing ones.

comments.author: MunchyCerealGuy
comments.body:
Game engines weren't built for agents. The closest thing we have is web dev code - Three.js and a few others. That's a real problem if you want your coding agent to use an engine, because its training data doesn't contain nearly enough Godot. So I wouldn't recommend Godot, or any traditional engine, if you're planning to co-work with a coding agent on your game. The agents just don't know enough about Godot, and even less about anything more niche.

Source: I spent six months trying to get my custom-built coding agent to use Godot and it constantly made dumb mistakes because it didn't understand how Godot worked. The moment I switched to an HTML-based stack, it was a 10x improvement.

replies.author: ul90
replies.body:
The current versions of Claude (Opus 5 / Fable 5.1) and ChatGPT (Astra) do know about Godot, they also do know how to implement GDScript and the GDExtensions in C++. By now, this is really working good. 

If you want quickly visible results, web browser target using three.js is good. But it has - of course - performance limitations. To use Godot, the AI agent has to configure your project accordingly, and bringing content and art into your project takes longer. But it's native and thus runs much faster.

replies.author: MunchyCerealGuy
replies.body: Yeah, I'm sure it can work well for individual games where you're directly overseeing the code for a single game, I was building an agentic workflow that could dynamically create any game (with monetization and multiplayer) for my creators based on their requests so creating a stable enough system with Godot as the engine choice didn't work fro me
